content.comment_body: Hello, How should this sensor be wired to the [product_name] analog input? [url] If I connect it as described, what could go wrong? W7 Signal GND => M, W8 GND => M, W9 Analog Out => I7, W10 Vcc => L+
That wiring is correct. However, your sensor has a 0-5 Volt output, while the [product_name] expects 0-10 Volt. It isn't a big issue, but you need to take care with how you scale the analog input.

I double-checked my wiring and turned on the power, but I'm not getting readings on the [product_name]. Also, the sensor started heating up, so I quickly disconnected it. I checked the connections again and they seem fine, so maybe the sensor isn't the type I thought. There’s a similar model with a 4-20mA output instead. [url] Hopefully I didn't damage anything. On the bright side, my previous test with PT-100 temperature sensors still works.

No component appears to be damaged. If your sensor uses a 4-20mA output, place a 500 Ohm resistor between the analog input and ground. For wiring: connect +24VDC to W10; connect W7 to the analog input (Ai7) of the [product_name]; and place a 500 Ohm resistor from Ai7 to -24VDC. This will convert the 4-20mA signal to a 2-10 Volt signal, but you will need to adjust the input scaling on the [product_name] accordingly.

Users encountered issues such as sensor heating and lack of readings, indicating confusion about wiring and sensor compatibility.
